title: Indian Ocean and its strategic importance
summary: A ready three-minute lecturette structure with facts you can use.
body: The Indian Ocean is the only ocean named after a country. It is the third largest ocean and carries much of the world's oil and container trade.
Key chokepoints are the Strait of Hormuz, Bab-el-Mandeb and the Strait of Malacca. Most of India's trade by volume and most of its oil imports travel by sea.

Piracy off Somalia, competition from extra-regional navies and the need to secure island territories such as the Andaman & Nicobar Islands. India describes itself as a 'first responder' and net security provider in the region.
SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region), now extended as MAHASAGAR; the Information Fusion Centre – Indian Ocean Region at Gurugram; and humanitarian missions such as Operation Rahat.
Whoever secures the Indian Ocean secures India's growth. A strong Navy and Coast Guard are central to that.
